question.worked_solution:
First, note that $x=0$ cannot be a solution. This is because if $x=0,$ then the rational term would be $\frac{27}{0},$ which is undefined because it has a zero denominator.

To solve the equation, we first multiply both sides by the denominator $x$ to get rid of the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{27}{x} & =9 \\ x\cdot \frac{27}{x} & =x\cdot 9 \\ \cancel{x}\cdot \frac{27}{\cancel{x}} & =9x \\ 27 & =9x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle:

$$
\begin{aligned}27 & =9x \\ \frac{27}{9} & =\frac{9x}{9} \\ 3 & =x\end{aligned}
$$

Since $x=3$ is different from $x=0$, we can accept it as a solution. Thus, the solution is $x=3.$
